Move all Deszo application panels, forms and dialogs to shadcn/ui. Preserve the current capabilities and workflow behavior, including React Flow editing, execution controls, recovery, history, Replay, Context chat and API/MCP authoring synchronization. Use the existing English product language.

The result is a separate local feature branch, `codex/shadcn-ui`, with the UI changes, relevant tests and documentation. Because `codex/shadcn-ui` already exists on origin and carries the ADR-0002 implementation commit, the delivery starting point before pilot execution must either:

1. explicitly accept the current head of `codex/shadcn-ui` (which includes the ADR-0002 commit and explicit-effort baseline) as the captured base commit to advance under an expected-ref condition; or
2. designate a fresh delivery branch from `main` (such as `codex/shadcn-ui-migration`), recording the branch absence condition.

Record the starting commit and the selected candidate before applying results. Merge and release remain separate actions.

Acceptance scope:
- The UI inventory covers the palette and application toolbar; workflow overview and node inspector; Map role editor and navigator; run, issue and Context panels; recovery controls; history and Replay; settings, workspace and workflow dialogs; external-run confirmation and Context chat.
- Application-owned buttons, inputs, selectors, dialogs, tabs and status surfaces use the agreed shadcn/ui components and shared theme tokens. Keep the React Flow canvas, port connections, selection, zoom/pan and nested navigation functional.
- Preserve save/load, validation, dirty-state handling, editor synchronization, run/stop/retry, task limits, Context behavior and all current configuration options, including reasoning effort.
- Verify keyboard navigation, labels, visible focus, dialog focus handling, disabled/busy states, error states and small-window overflow on the affected surfaces.
- Run the frontend build, appropriate runtime/contract regression checks and documentation checks. Add meaningful UI interaction coverage for the changed flows using the fixture runtime. Record browser screenshots and a desktop smoke result for behavior that depends on Tauri.
- Produce the final diff, actual check evidence, known limitations and an Analyst verdict linked to the original task. This brief itself does not claim the pilot passed.

Migrate owned controls to shadcn/ui and shared theme tokens, preserving the React Flow canvas, graph interactions, existing English text, functional contracts and reasoning-effort settings. Preserve the Vite local-runtime connection plugin, Tauri behavior and @xyflow/react styling.

Read docs/IMPLEMENTATION_MAP.md, docs/PIPELINE_EXECUTION.md and both docs/schemas/spec-section-index.schema.json and docs/schemas/implementation-map.schema.json. The round-recovery documents are FORMAT examples only; do not copy their fictional business requirements.

Write SPEC.md, spec-index.json and implementation-map.json. Use exactly ## ID headings for every indexed section, all headings indexed, stable acyclic IDs, requirementRefs limited to normative REQ-/CONTRACT- IDs. Every task needs its full transitive normative closure as explicit spec inputs AND readScopes, including test-case/check obligations. dependsOn entries are {taskId, milestone:"accepted"}, never section IDs or strings.

Allowed executor role IDs: implementer, test-author, junior-analyst, verification. The code-reviewer role reviews code and implementation documentation; test-reviewer independently reviews tests and test evidence. The analyst role owns substantive decisions and verification triage. verification is an engine utility, not a provider.

Plan bounded file groups. Give package.json/package-lock.json, theme/global CSS, Vite/TS setup and each shared source file exactly one owner; order every later task that modifies or consumes those files after its accepted producer. Test author and developer use separate task directories and approved interfaces.

Include an accepted documentation task owned by junior-analyst after the UI implementation. Its outputs describe the resulting UI and developer commands. Do not delegate requirement meaning to that role.

Include TASK-UI-EVIDENCE owned by test-author after ALL UI source and test-script outputs have been accepted. It runs node scripts/shadcn-pilot-check.mjs --ui-only --evidence-dir docs/pilots/shadcn-ui-evidence and captures docs/pilots/shadcn-ui-evidence/report.json, main.png, dialogs.png and small-window.png as a declared fileSet reviewed by test-reviewer. These are generated from the complete accepted UI, not hand-authored screenshots. Include this task and its evidence in final verification dependencies/candidate paths. Check-runner scratch directories are deleted; screenshots generated only during CHECK execution would otherwise be lost.

Create a final TASK-VERIFY utility task that depends on and consumes every accepted output needed in the complete candidate. Its candidate paths must include every changed/new deliverable. Do not include node_modules, dist, reports or temporary files as deliverables.

The approved final candidate check must run node scripts/shadcn-pilot-check.mjs (source candidate, requiredExitCode 0, timeoutSeconds 600). The wrapper installs pinned dependencies, builds, runs runtime regressions, documentation checks and npm run test:ui, then bundles the runtime. The foundation task must add the required browser-test dependency/script; test-author must provide meaningful fixture-runtime browser interaction coverage and screenshot evidence. Do not create test:ui as an empty stub.

test:ui must honor DESZO_UI_EVIDENCE_DIR (relative to the project), write report.json with schemaVersion 1, nonempty scenarios [{id,status:"passed"}] covering the approved scenario IDs, and screenshots ["main.png","dialogs.png","small-window.png"]. Write the three actual browser PNG screenshots in that directory. Include real viewport/interaction/expectation details and source-file digests in the report. The wrapper validates report presence, all scenario statuses and PNG signatures; The test reviewer judges coverage/evidence and the code reviewer judges implementation/visual behavior.

Fresh task/check directories have no node_modules. Give tasks that need npm/builds explicit scratch writeScopes for node_modules/**, dist/**, dist-runtime/**, .deszo/** and *.tsbuildinfo. The verification task must allow those NEW scratch paths. npm ci must not modify existing tracked inputs; never change source from a checker. All CHECK commands run independently in fresh directories, so keep full-candidate steps in the one wrapper.

Capture representative browser screenshots and machine-readable assertions for critical UI flows, accessible labels/focus/dialog behavior, busy/disabled/error states, and small-window overflow. A browser result cannot prove a desktop-only behavior. Record the remaining Tauri desktop smoke for the operator after candidate application; do not claim it already happened.

Provider invocations are bounded to 600 seconds. Split implementation into feasible tasks. Allow at most three task attempts and three failed verification cycles. On unknown triage preserve evidence and pause. Do not weaken requirements/checks to pass.

The source base is pinned by the prepared manifest. During documentation authoring write ONLY SPEC.md, spec-index.json and implementation-map.json. Never edit app source, package files or the pilot tooling in this directory. Return a concise summary of semantic decisions and remaining risks.

Before returning, run node "C:\\Users\\jusse\\.codex\\worktrees\\shadcn-ui-pilot\\deszo_agent_orche\\.deszo\\pilots\\shadcn-ui\\validate-documents.mjs". Correct schema/closure/role errors until it passes. The validator also detects changes to the pinned project; do not modify the validator or its manifest.

Independent review roles: implementer and junior-analyst tasks require code-reviewer review criteria; test-author tasks, including TASK-UI-EVIDENCE, require test-reviewer criteria. A task that changes both production code and tests requires both reviewers. Use distinct acceptance criterion IDs and the exact role IDs code-reviewer and test-reviewer; the old reviewer role does not exist. The two requirement-review slots and both final technical-review slots must approve independently before advancing.

Review requirements as code-reviewer: complete business/UI scope, interface preservation, implementation feasibility, bounded task decomposition, ordered file ownership and documentation consistency. Testability and test design have a separate test-reviewer.
